note: The graph spec's decisions, each with a short title, its date and one line on why (editor spec §51, spec_decisions_explained). The title and date come from the decision's own id in graph-spec.gql. This file holds the why. test/graph-spec-readable.test.js holds the two together.

why.2026-10-04 A removal that meets a change: A removal beside a change cannot be applied safely, so a person settles it.
why.2026-10-04 Cached status and balances ar: A figure kept for speed must be checked against the facts it came from.
why.2026-10-04 Calibration, source reliabili: Nothing is typed in by hand, so these figures always follow the claims that were confirmed or refuted.
why.2026-10-04 Contested removals cover rela: A link can be removed too, and an else that swallows events does harm at any depth.
why.2026-10-04 Decisions live in their own g: The record of why stays apart from the thing it explains, so neither one is edited by accident.
why.2026-10-04 Doubtful statements are claim: A doubtful statement is kept and rated, not dropped, and a word never hides how unsure it is.
why.2026-10-04 Each graph carries its own sc: A graph can be checked anywhere, and two engines give the same answer.
why.2026-10-04 GQL is the notation for graph: One authored notation means no two copies of the rules can drift apart.
why.2026-10-04 Issued documents keep a paylo: A hash proves a document is the one that was issued.
why.2026-10-04 Joining documents graphs neve: Joining two graphs must not lose what either one says.
why.2026-10-04 Joins cover three or more doc: People join more than two graphs, and revisions and processes need the same care.
why.2026-10-04 Lenses group nodes by rule, a: A reader sees a few big items first and follows a link for detail.
why.2026-10-04 Process sub-flows follow SCXM: An existing standard gives rules that are already tested, until our own are proved.
why.2026-10-04 The conformance suite is part: An implementation is conforming only if it passes the same cases as every other.
why.2026-10-04 The graph spec model aligns w: Other tools already understand the standards, so the graph is easier to share.
why.2026-10-04 Two claims combine as likelih: Combining two claims must not look surer than they are.
why.2026-10-05 A graph may name a shared sch: Graphs that share kinds declare them once, so they cannot disagree.
why.2026-10-05 A models proposal must come f: A proposal can be traced to exactly what the model was shown.
why.2026-10-05 An AI is fed graphs by a view: What a model saw is on record, so its proposals can be checked against it.
why.2026-10-05 An AI writes only claims and: A person decides what enters the graph, and tools check what an AI offers.
why.2026-10-05 Judgements are decisions with: A judgement shows what it rested on, and a person makes the call.
why.2026-10-05 Knowledge graphs are checked: Any system can store, show and check a graph without a database.
why.2026-10-05 Paths are nodes, and altitude: A reader can move from the overview to the detail without losing the way.
why.2026-10-05 Sub-flows never nest in a loo: A sub-flow in a loop never ends clearly, and one named flow is easy to follow.
why.2026-10-06 Relationships are named by sh: Queries match a short stable name, and people read the phrase.
why.2026-10-16 The graph spec adopts W3C PRO: A standard for who made what already exists, so tools can read ours.
why.2026-10-15 AI proposals remove and chang: Roger asked for removals and changes through the language itself, and a rejected idea must not linger.
why.2026-10-16 A model is cleared by its des: Each change can be accepted or rejected alone.
why.2026-10-06 The graph spec describes itse: The spec is checked by the same tools as any other graph.
why.2026-10-06 A graph block may leave out I: A block of things and links reads like a data file, and any engine still loads it.
why.2026-10-07 A missing comma between graph: A small slip is reported and fixed, and does not fail the whole block.
why.2026-10-07 A link type written without i: A missing colon must never turn a link into a link of any type.
why.2026-10-06 A things name in a graph bloc: One name per thing is simpler than a nickname and an id.
why.2026-10-10 SET never changes a nodes id: Links and records point to an id, so changing it would break them.
why.2026-10-10 A nodes id is always text: One kind of id reads the same in every library.
why.2026-10-10 Every route into a graph engi: Every engine sees the same checked text.
why.2026-10-10 An engine keeps a blocks comm: The writer's notes survive, and the engine still gets valid text.
why.2026-10-06 A graph is a draft until lock: A new graph can grow freely, and locking records what it turned out to be.
why.2026-10-11 Grafeo is the compatibility r: The readers are proved against a real engine, but nobody needs it to read or check.
why.2026-10-11 Text in a graph block reads b: Text means the same to the readers as to any GQL engine.
why.2026-10-11 A figure missing a fact it re: A missing fact must never be quietly counted as zero.
why.2026-10-20 Trust on joined graphs, from: A claim from a graph nobody trusts is flagged, not counted.
why.2026-10-06 Completeness is declared in t: Roger asked for the spec to be checked for completeness through the graph itself.
why.2026-10-06 An id is local unless prefixe: Roger asked for both, made explicit, with a way to force a local id to say so.
why.2026-10-06 A Deferred node parks known w: Work to do later is kept in the graph and not lost in a note.
why.2026-10-10 A note on a thing is written: Notes stay beside what they explain, and read as plain Markdown.
why.2026-10-11 Notes and tool-hint lines sha: Mixing a note and a hint must not cut the note off from its element.
why.2026-10-11 Note text drops trailing whit: Invisible spaces must not change what a note says.
why.2026-10-10 Extensions to the graph langu: Roger confirmed three homes, so an extension has one clear place.
